tob-10792: Manly P. Hall, the great popularizer of esoteric wisdom, retells the ancient story of fire as a symbol of the human soul. He draws on Egyptian, Greek, and Christian sources to show how the ‘sacred flame’ was guarded by initiates in mystery schools. Written when Hall was only twenty-one, it launched a lifetime of work on hidden teachings.
tob-0092: Reginald Scot’s 1584 book was the first full broadside against the witch scare — he laid bare the jugglers’ tricks and held that supposed witches were mazed old women, not Satan’s servants. His debunking so nettled King James that the king had copies burned. It stands as a landmark of doubt.
tob-4092: This rendering of the Elder Edda gives the old Norse lays in English — the seeress’s foretelling of world’s end, the High One’s sayings, the lays of heroes and dragons. A workmanlike version that served readers for generations. The poems keep the raw voice of the Viking mind.
tob-0192: This set gathers Hindu Tantra books — the writ of goddess-worship, spell-words, and holy doings that bloomed in medieval India. The Tantras teach freedom through the body and its fires, not away from them. The volume opens a little-known world of Indian godliness to English readers.
tob-4192: Anuruddha’s Compendium — the Abhidhammattha Sangaha — is the classic handbook of Buddhist Abhidhamma, the schoolmen’s chart of mind and matter. C. A. F. Rhys Davids’s Englishing opened this close philosophy to western readers. Her notes light the way through its thickets. The book stays the standard English door to Abhidhamma.
cia-0000105892: A July 1965 report on the decision to cancel a scheduled event for President Sukarno, officially for reasons of health and security. In the tense politics of 1965 Indonesia, even a cancellation carried meaning — rumors about Sukarno's health fed the power struggle around him. The CIA read such moves for clues about who really held control.
cia-0000107492: An April 1966 study of Communist China's balance of payments from 1950 to 1965 — the money flowing in and out of Mao's China. Trade figures revealed what propaganda hid: how the economy really performed through the Great Leap Forward and its aftermath. The document is economic detective work on a country that published no honest statistics.
cia-0000117892: An October 1972 study of Cuban international activities hostile to American interests. Havana's reach extended from Africa to Latin America — troops, agents, and revolutionaries. The report catalogs a decade of Cuban activism as Washington saw it: a small island punching far above its weight.
cia-0000126892: A July 1977 report on South Africa's uranium enrichment program — part of the title deleted. Enrichment is the step that turns uranium into bomb fuel, and Pretoria was mastering it in secret. The document tracks the technical heart of apartheid's nuclear ambitions.
cia-0000132292: Situation Report 601: the opening moves of the ground war — Saddam's forces, the truncated title suggests, about to be overrun. After weeks of bombing, the coalition's armor rolled forward. The document captures the hundred-hour war's first hours: the end, beginning.
cia-0000132592: Item 14 in the August 1960 series: Cuba possibly restoring a Shell refinery to British-Dutch ownership — the truncated title cuts off the details. The oil war had its feints and reversals. The document is the refinery, bargained: the crude politics of crude oil.
cia-0000135892: A 1954 general and specific file — subject deleted — on instruction in nerve war against individuals, the garbled title suggests. Psychological warfare, person by person. The entry is the method: the nerves, attacked.
cia-0000135992: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN with views on IDEN B's reasoning about communist actions — the truncated title cuts off the details. Identities were coded; reasoning was analyzed. The entry is the analysis: the reasoning, weighed — the identity, masked.
cia-0000136192: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for ONTRICH reporting communication between SEMANTIC and SEQ — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The cryptonyms conversed. The entry is the link: the communication, noted.
cia-0000140392: A 1957 letter to and from a deleted person on the military application of hypnotism. The mind-control correspondence. The document is the letter: the hypnosis, militarized.
un-sc-res-92: Security Council Resolution 92, adopted in 1951. The Council's sixth year. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-392: Security Council Resolution 392, adopted in June 1976 — the Soweto resolution, condemning South Africa's killing of demonstrators in the township uprising. The Council answered apartheid's bullets with the world's censure. The resolution is the condemnation: the massacre, denounced.
un-sc-res-492: Security Council Resolution 492, adopted in 1981 — aligned. The deliberations continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-992: Security Council Resolution 992, cataloged with the year 1991 — the numbering belongs to 1995, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1292: Security Council Resolution 1292, adopted in 2000 — aligned. The deliberations continued. The designation and year are preserved; the act belongs to the text.
cia-0000135692: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135692. The pre-invasion archive. The document is the archive: the brigade, before.
cia-0000136692: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136692, the archive's date uncertain. The roughly dated papers. The document is the roughness: the date, soft.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d92: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 3, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 92. The next day, London wrote again. The message is the persistence: the correspondence, daily.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d192: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 6, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 192. London's letter. The message is the correspondence: the prime minister, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d292: A memorandum by the United States Chiefs of Staff, November 23, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 292. The American planners' paper. The memo is the planners': the chiefs, American.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d392: The Secretary of State to the President, November 29, 1943 — Document 392. A second that day. The memo is the doubling: the day, crowded.
biographies-of-working-men-pg6492: Science writer Grant Allen profiles men who rose from humble beginnings through talent and hard work — engineers, inventors, and explorers among them. Each short life is meant to show what determination can achieve without wealth or rank. Written in the hopeful Victorian spirit of self-help, the book celebrates the dignity of labor and the power of perseverance.
arxiv-2605-08892: Pascal's triangle hides a matrix with a rich algebraic life, and the Riordan group is the natural home for such triangular arrays. Helena Cobo studies the Pascal matrix inside the multivariate Riordan group, working out its group-theoretic properties. The 2026 paper is pure algebra on a classical object.
arxiv-2605-09192: Teaching a robot a skill from demonstrations works until the plan meets reality. Yang Zhou, Zihan Dong, Zhenting Wang, and colleagues prefer evidence over plans: online trajectory verification for skill distillation, checking each move as it happens. The 2026 paper is robotics that trusts its sensors more than its scripts.
arxiv-2605-09692: Language agents that bind causal states to actions may control themselves better — or so the theory goes. Xiao Jia puts it to the test, asking whether causal state binding predicts action control in language agents. The 2026 paper is cognitive science for AI agents.
arxiv-2605-09892: LEO satellite-to-ground optical links usually assume independent fading — a convenient fiction. Xinyan Xie, Xuesong Wang, Jinghua Zhang, and colleagues revisit the assumption with a state-coupled joint fading model. The 2026 paper is satellite communications facing correlated fading reality.
arxiv-2605-09992: Speculative decoding models learn — but what exactly do they learn? Attention drift reveals the answer. Doğaç Eldenk, Payal Mohapatra, Yigitcan Comlek, and colleagues investigate what autoregressive speculative decoding models learn. The 2026 paper is efficient inference, interpreted. It watches the drafters learn.
plos-pone-0003392: Statisticians compared anti-bias tools for gene hunting in this 2008 paper. When study groups mix people of different ancestries, false gene-disease links appear, a problem called population stratification. The authors tested several statistical methods that correct for this hidden structure in population-based association studies, giving geneticists a practical guide to which correction holds up best.
plos-pone-0003492: Vision researchers found the eyes' position changes what the brain sees in this 2008 primate study. Recording from inferotemporal cortex, the object-recognition area of the ventral visual stream, they showed that where the eyes point modulates the neural response. The result means the brain's picture of objects is anchored partly to the viewer, not purely to the object.
plos-pone-0003592: Immunologists found tiny loop differences steering T-cell fate in this 2008 paper. Two microRNAs, mir-181a-1 and mir-181c, share nearly identical sequences yet act differently in early T-cell development, and the team traced the difference to nucleotides in their precursor loops. The loops, not just the mature sequence, tune what these regulators do.
plos-pone-0003692: In 2008, Hung and Colicos found star-shaped brain cells guiding growing nerves. Waves of calcium sweeping through astrocytes steered neuronal growth cones toward distant zones of brain activity. The result gives support cells an active directing role in wiring the developing nervous system.
plos-pone-0003792: Seitz and Watanabe asked if background learning is ever truly background in this 2008 paper. Their experiments probed task-irrelevant learning, where the brain picks up stimuli it was told to ignore. The results question whether any learning is fully irrelevant to what the mind is doing.
plos-pone-0003892: In 2008, Tsuchiya, Kawasaki, and Oya read faces straight from the brain. Using electrodes placed inside patients' heads, they decoded face information across time, frequency, and space. The direct recordings reveal how the brain's face system divides its labor.
plos-pone-0003992: In 2008, Zhang, Xu, and Peng found a second virus slowing the first. Among HIV-infected former plasma donors, hepatitis C coinfection meant slower disease progression. The team tracked how hepatitis C altered HIV replication in these patients. The counterintuitive result complicates the simple story of always-harmful viral coinfection.
plos-pone-0004092: In 2008, Ohazama, Johnson, and Ota found a protein tuning signals outside cells. Lrp4 shaped how signaling pathways blend beyond the cell surface. The receptor-related protein worked hard during development. The neat finding moves signal mixing out of the cell's interior.
plos-pone-0004192: In 2009, Mavromatis, Ivanova, and Anderson sequenced a salt-loving heat bug. The genome of the anaerobic thermohalophilic bacterium Halothermothrix orenii was decoded. Pulled from a Tunisian salt lake, it thrives where few can. The blueprint expands the tree of life.
plos-pone-0004292: In 2009, a US team found a metabolic disorder inviting cancer. PKU mice showed stronger tumor effects. The PKU model's chemistry favored tumor growth. The link urges cancer watchfulness in PKU. The mouse work flags a hidden risk of the disorder.
plos-pone-0358592: Rural hospice nurses do heartbreaking work far from support. This national study identified predictors of work engagement among rural and remote nurses providing hospice, palliative, and end-of-life care. The predictors show what keeps these nurses going — and what burns them out and drives them away.
plos-pone-0355492: Children born with HIV face a lifetime of treatment — and drug resistance looms over every missed dose. This cohort study examined adherence to antiretroviral therapy and the impact of drug resistance on evolving viral suppression in children and adolescents with perinatal HIV. The results directly guide pediatric HIV care strategies.
plos-pone-0353992: Small businesses drown in competing CSR frameworks they can’t afford to implement. This paper rationalized the manifold dimensions and aspects of corporate social responsibility toward sustainable business performance in small and medium enterprises. The streamlined model shows small firms which responsibility efforts genuinely pay off.
plos-pone-0357592: Monkey jack fruit pulp — Artocarpus lacucha — may naturally preserve fish. This study tested its functional application as a natural preservative for raw pangasius, measuring effects on quality, safety, and storage stability. The fruit extract extended shelf life without synthetic chemicals.
plos-pone-0357292: PEGylated peptide drugs need rigorous purity checks — free polyethylene glycols are the impurity to watch. This paper presented quantitative analysis of those glycols using reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography with charged aerosol detection. The validated method guards the quality of an important drug class.
plos-pone-0357492: Diagnosing middle ear disease from otoscopy videos alone is notoriously hard. This multi-center study integrated otoscopy videos with tympanometry measurements using confidence-guided AI, validated with external paired cohorts. The fusion of sight and pressure data meaningfully improves diagnostic accuracy.
plos-pone-0357092: Overtaking on rural two-lane highways is among driving’s deadliest maneuvers. This paper modeled overtaking duration by integrating survival analysis with machine learning. The model’s predictions inform road design and driver-assistance systems aimed at making the pass safer.
plos-pone-0357392: Husbands profoundly shape whether contraceptive needs go unmet — yet standard measures ignore them. This paper incorporated husbands’ influence into unmet need estimation using a modified revised algorithm. The more honest measure should reshape family planning programs.
plos-pone-0354892: Pollution-induced flashover on high-voltage insulators can black out entire regions. This machine learning framework predicted equivalent salt deposit density on glass insulators, with SHAP-based feature optimization revealing what matters. The model helps utilities prevent failures before the lights go out.
plos-pone-0356992: Cataract surgery can trigger macular edema that threatens the vision it just restored. This paper tested the efficacy of a one-week course of topical bromfenac combined with corticosteroid for preventing pseudophakic cystoid macular edema. The short regimen protects the retina when it’s most vulnerable.
plos-pone-0355692: Chronic back pain demands rehab that treats both mind and muscle. This study combined pain neuroscience education with flexi-bar stabilization exercises, measuring effects on functional disability, pain, and abdominal muscle geometry. The combined approach addresses what patients believe about pain — and how their cores actually work.
plos-pone-0356392: Rural Ethiopian women drop out of the maternal care continuum at alarming rates. This multilevel analysis measured the level of completion and its determinants among rural women in East Shoa Zone. The findings pinpoint exactly where the continuum breaks — and what would keep mothers in care.
plos-pone-0355292: Aligning LiDAR point clouds — registration — is fundamental to 3D mapping. This paper presented a strengthened soft-point registration network for the task. The improved network aligns scans more robustly, sharpening everything from autonomous driving maps to digital twins.
plos-pone-0353692: Discovering new composite materials is slow — but active learning can close the loop. This paper applied graph-theoretic active learning to the closed-loop discovery of stochastic heterogeneous composites. The intelligent search strategy finds promising materials with far fewer experiments than brute-force screening.
plos-pone-0356292: Seeking mental health help in New York City looks different depending on who you are. This paper examined how intersecting identities shape informal and formal support use. The intersectional findings reveal that race, class, gender, and immigration status combine to open or close doors to care.
plos-pone-0355792: Diabetes might raise the risk of jaw joint disorders — a connection hiding in population data. This nationwide population-based study examined the association between diabetes mellitus and temporomandibular disorder risk. The findings suggest dentists and diabetologists should be watching each other’s patients.
plos-pone-0354292: Observational studies can’t prove causation — yet scientists keep making causal claims. This paper asked who is more likely to do so, examining author experience, team size, cultural background, and gender in scientific framing. The findings expose the human factors behind one of science’s most consequential bad habits.
plos-pone-0355392: Removing phenolic compounds from natural organic matter — for cleaner water analysis — needs the right chemistry. This paper evaluated the efficacy and specificity of PVPP for that removal. The validated method gives water scientists a reliable tool for isolating what they need to measure.
plos-pone-0355192: Online videos might teach diabetes self-care better than pamphlets. This randomized controlled trial tested web-based educational videos for enhancing diabetes knowledge and empowerment among type 2 patients in primary care. The findings show whether digital education genuinely empowers patients to manage their disease.
europmc-pmc2800192: To study immune cells in the dish, scientists coax a lab cell line called THP-1 into behaving like macrophages. This 2010 paper identifies reliable markers of that transformation, both in THP-1 cells and in macrophages grown from human blood monocytes. The marker list gives researchers a checklist to confirm their cell models are working properly before running experiments.
europmc-pmc2811892: During the 2009 pandemic flu, some patients crashed while others recovered, and this paper looked for an early warning in the blood. The authors found that severe cases showed a surge of Th1 and Th17 inflammatory signals, a hypercytokinemia signature. Measuring this immune overreaction could flag patients heading for trouble. The study linked immune excess to pandemic flu severity.
europmc-pmc2829492: Cancer cells addicted to sugar fermentation can resist chemotherapy, and this 2010 paper finds a way to break the resistance. The authors show that blocking lactate dehydrogenase-A re-sensitizes taxol-resistant cancer cells to the drug. Targeting the Warburg effect restored the treatment's punch. The strategy links tumor metabolism to drug response.
europmc-pmc2885492: Feeling sick starts in the brain, and this 2009 paper traces the spark. The authors map the neural origins of sickness feelings in the brain's response to inflammation. Their imaging work reveals the circuitry. The study explains why inflammation feels so awful.
europmc-pmc2945792: Predicting microRNA targets got sharper in this 2010 paper. The authors' broad modeling predicts working non-conserved and non-canonical target sites. Their wider net catches real targets older tools miss. The work improved a core genomics task. Gene hunters still use its predictions today.
europmc-pmc300692: Blocking one protein can starve kidney tumors. This 2003 paper shows shutting down HIF2alpha halts tumors missing the VHL brake. The authors reveal the weak spot. Their work launched a drug class. HIF2alpha blockers later reached kidney patients. The 2019 Nobel honored this oxygen pathway.
europmc-pmc3018492: BPA levels swing during pregnancy. This 2011 paper tracks how urinary BPA rises and falls in pregnant women. The authors reveal the swings and their drivers. Their work informs exposure science. Canned food proved the biggest source. One urine test cannot capture the exposure.
europmc-pmc3061292: Brain data analysis got a manual. This 2011 guide walks through EEG and MEG analysis in the SPM8 software. The authors lead readers step by step. Their chapter trained a generation. Students still learn SPM from these pages. The guide demystifies tricky statistics.
europmc-pmc3101192: TB's metabolism got mapped. This 2011 paper charts how the tuberculosis germ's chemistry steers growth and drug response. The authors reveal the wiring. Their work points to new TB drugs. Starved germs turn drug-tolerant, they find. Metabolic blockers may shorten treatment.
europmc-pmc6558092: PD-1 is a brake pedal on T cells that tumors exploit to switch the immune attack off. Drugs that block PD-1 release the brake, letting T cells strike - a revolution in cancer care. This review surveys where PD-1 blockade works, where it fails, and how it pairs with other treatments, charting the state of one of immunotherapy's biggest success stories.
europmc-pmc6678092: Mitochondria are the cell's power stations - but they also run signaling, immunity, and death programs. This review tours their roles in health and disease: energy, of course, plus the newer jobs. When power stations falter, the fallout spans diabetes to neurodegeneration.
europmc-pmc6730892: About 700 American women die yearly from pregnancy - and Black women die at far higher rates. Analyzing CDC surveillance from 2007 to 2016, this report documents the racial and ethnic disparities in pregnancy-related deaths. The numbers are a moral emergency hiding in plain sight.
europmc-pmc6751792: Testing one drug at a time is slow - master protocols test many at once. This landscape review maps basket trials (one drug, many cancers), umbrella trials (many drugs, one cancer), and platform trials that add or drop arms mid-study. The new designs squeeze more answers from fewer patients.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1092: The wildlife agency inherited a farm problem in 2007: fields handed over from the farm department that did not fit refuge life. GAO's report says the Fish and Wildlife Service needed room to bend the rules for these odd-lot lands. The findings pit the plow's legacy against the refuge's mission — and ask for flexibility to square them.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-892: Every responder deserved a health check in 2007 — GAO's report says the health agency had to guarantee screening for all of them. The findings press HHS to close the coverage gaps. The report's moral is plain: the nation sent them in; the nation owes them the follow-up.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-592: Tagging every farm animal was stumbling in 2007 — GAO's report says the animal-ID system needed key fixes before it could track disease fast enough. The findings list the implementation snags holding it back. The report's logic is plain: you cannot quarantine what you cannot trace.
openalex-w7206207892: Caring for a sick relative at home is hard, and families often feel unprepared. This study set out to learn what home caregivers struggle with most, then built an educational tool to help them. Based on qualitative research from 2019, the authors designed teaching material aimed at daily home care. Practical and humane, it treats family caregivers as learners who deserve real support.
openalex-w7204989892: Underground water feeds towns across Brazil's dry northeast, but rock aquifers can be polluted. This study maps how vulnerable a crystalline aquifer system is to contamination in Varzea Alegre, Ceara. The authors trace the geology and the human pressures on the water below. A technical hydrogeology study with direct stakes for everyone who drinks from a well in the region.
openalex-w7204442892: Farm soils in the tropics trap phosphorus, a key plant food, where crops cannot reach it. This farm-science study tested how different phosphate fertilizers free up phosphorus over time in soils of varied texture. The authors measured which sources kept the nutrient open to roots longest. Hands-on soil science for growers battling tropical ground.
openalex-w7204226692: In the Amazon, the river sets the prices. This case study looks at a small building-materials retailer in Tefe, Amazonas, and how the Solimoes River's seasonal rise and fall shapes its purchasing, costs, and profits. The authors show hydrology driving economics. A vivid example of business at the mercy of the waters.
openalex-w7204251392: Tocantins created a formal penal police career, and this study asks whether the upgrade worked. The authors investigate how institutionalizing and valuing the career affected the quality of sentence enforcement in the state. The research links professional dignity to public outcomes. A public-security study of what happens when a job gets the respect it was missing.
openalex-w7204237392: Bullying poisons school life for victims and bystanders alike. This article offers a practical guide: how to spot bullying and how to build a culture of peace and tolerance in its place. The authors cover the emotional, social, and academic damage, then turn to solutions. A compassionate handbook for schools ready to act.
openalex-w7204128392: Social media turned campaigning into a free-for-all, and this article asks how democracy survives it. The authors study digital political ads and electoral integrity through constitutional and comparative law: fake news, paid boosts, and the line between speech and sabotage. A legal study of elections in the age of the feed.
openalex-w7138893692: How long does the coronavirus live on hospital room surfaces? This study swabbed the rooms of COVID patients in airy single rooms, pairing gene tests with live-virus culture. The team sized up the true infection risk. A germ-control study of surfaces versus air.
openalex-w4416399692: Backyard chickens can carry drug-resistant germs to their keepers. This study tested backyard broiler chickens and their human contacts for multidrug-resistant Klebsiella. The authors typed the strains and resistance genes. A One Health study of resistance hopping from coop to kitchen.
pmc-13430592: A 2026 cell biology paper showing that AP-1B — a protein complex that sorts cargo inside cells — controls multiple levels of proliferation and differentiation in mouse enteroids, lab-grown mini-guts. Getting gut stem cells to divide and specialize correctly depends on this sorting machinery. The finding matters for gut development and disease models.
pmc-13505392: A 2026 systematic review of digital psychological interventions for youth with neurological disorders. Apps and online programs could reach young patients where clinics can't. The review assesses what works.
pmc-13468792: A 2026 paper showing Trem2 negatively regulates the mTOR-PKCα axis to protect against Toxoplasma-induced adverse pregnancy outcomes. The immune receptor's brake on inflammation saved pregnancies. The mechanism is a therapeutic hint.
pmc-13523692: A 2026 materials paper on an energy-gradient strategy for triplet-pair separation in singlet-fission oligomers — relevant to next-generation solar cells. The gradient drove the separation. The strategy is the advance.
pmc-13529192: This 2026 Mendelian randomization study examined causal relationships between the oral-gut microbiome and bone neoplasm-related phenotypes. Microbes may influence bone tumors. The causal analysis is the approach.
pmc-13517992: A 2026 case report of transaminitis — liver enzyme elevation — from duloxetine. The antidepressant's hepatic effect was documented. The case warns prescribers.
pmc-13514692: A 2026 study of generative AI dependence's impact on university students' creativity — critical thinking as mediator, thinking style as moderator. The AI-creativity link was dissected. The mediation model is the insight.
pmc-13490892: In this 2026 veterinary vaccine paper, an indigenous Salmonella gallinarum ghost vaccine was developed and evaluated for fowl typhoid control in poultry. The local vaccine served local needs. The evaluation is the evidence.
pmc-13494692: A 2026 medicinal chemistry paper designing, synthesizing, and in silico profiling pyridyl-thiazole-thiosemicarbazones as anti-trypanosomatid agents. The parasite killers were computationally vetted. The design is the pipeline.
pmc-13487692: In this 2026 radiation oncology paper, lower lobe dose parameters correlated with radiation pneumonitis in definitive lung cancer radiotherapy. The dose-volume link was quantified. The correlation guides planning.
pmc-13470592: A 2026 case report of sclerosing atypical lipomatous tumor with myxomatous features presenting in the plantar heel. The foot's fatty tumor was characterized. The case documents the rarity.
pmc-13463492: A 2026 veterinary paper with seminal analysis and testicular RNA sequencing of a low-fertility ram. The ram's infertility was molecularly profiled. The sequencing is the diagnostic depth.
pmc-13446592: In this 2026 cardiology paper, PKA-mediated proteasome activation protected against cardiac remodeling and heart failure during systolic overload. The protein-degrading machinery was the protector. The activation is the mechanism.
pmc-13439492: In this 2026 reproductive biology paper, anethole's effects on meiotic resumption and oxidative balance during in vitro maturation of ovine oocytes were studied. The fennel compound aided egg maturation. The effects are the finding.
pmc-13416392: A 2026 qualitative investigation exploring parent support needs during and after adolescent suicide crisis emergency department visits. The parents' needs were voiced. The investigation guides ED support.
pmc-13436692: In this 2026 review, light-dependent processes in algae across scales were examined — from cellular physiology to ecological organization. The algal light biology was synthesized. The review spans the scales.
pmc-13348492: In this 2026 Australian national linked data cohort study, longitudinal patterns of chronic hepatitis B care and treatment adherence were examined. The care cascade was tracked. The patterns reveal the gaps.
pmc-13439692: In this 2026 C. elegans paper, transcriptional feedback targeting Wnt pathway components revealed hidden heterogeneity in seam cell lineages. The worm's stem cells differed. The heterogeneity is the developmental insight.
pmc-13451092: A 2026 Polish study of empathy, access, and delays as determinants of oncology care satisfaction in academic and nonacademic hospitals. The cancer patients' satisfaction drivers were identified. The determinants guide improvement.
pmc-13534492: A 2026 machine learning paper: activity-cliff awareness enabled robust graph learning for molecular property prediction. The chemistry-aware AI was hardened. The awareness is the innovation.
pmc-13473992: A 2026 education paper on how children learned complex environmental concepts through digital storytelling — divergent pathways to knowledge and stewardship intention. The stories taught differently. The pathways are the finding.
pmc-13465092: A 2026 paper with integrated molecular docking and molecular dynamics revealing potential antimicrobial metabolites from the sea cucumber Holothuria scabra. The marine metabolites were computationally screened. The revealing is the bioprospecting.
pmc-13426392: A 2026 paper: diabetes treatment altered the subgingival microbiome in type 2 diabetes patients. The drugs reshaped the mouth's bacteria. The alteration is the finding.
pmc-13639192: This 2026 paper forecasted extreme temperature events by Hankel-augmented contrastive learning. The AI predicted the heat extremes. The forecasting is the climate tool.
pmc-13528392: A 2026 narrative review on how artificial intelligence is disrupting medical knowledge and evaluation. The AI's epistemic upheaval was surveyed. The review is the field's reckoning.
pmc-13512592: This 2026 quantum computing paper presented execution-aware segmented modeling of temporally correlated flux-induced phase noise in quantum circuits. The noise was modeled precisely. The modeling serves error mitigation.
pmc-13461492: A 2026 intact-class quasi-experimental study of a need-supportive digital sports platform and physical activity outcomes in university physical education (the title is truncated). The digital platform's activity boost was tested. The study is the education evidence.
arxiv-2606-15992: Coaches usually analyze tennis strokes by eye, which misses fine details of movement. This paper uses MediaPipe — Google's free body-tracking tool — to map players' joint positions and study the biomechanics of different strokes at once. One model analyzes serves, forehands, and backhands from ordinary video, giving coaches data they could not see before.
arxiv-2606-16292: Modern AI products pile up software components with tangled licenses, and one violation can sink a company. The "AI Supply Chain Galaxy" is a 3D visual analytics tool that maps those dependencies and flags license-compliance risks. The paper presents the visualization system for teams managing legal risk in AI software stacks.
arxiv-2606-16492: The Lyapunov equation is central to control theory — it tells engineers whether a system is stable. This paper studies the equation when the state matrix is in "companion form," a special structured layout that appears in many control problems. The author exploits that structure for sharper results, targeting control theorists.
arxiv-2606-16592: Logs record what software did — and sometimes you need to undo exactly what happened. This paper develops closure-preserving rate–distortion theory for reversible logging: compressing logs aggressively while keeping the ability to reverse operations. It targets information theorists and systems engineers building auditable, undoable software.
